footer.aboutText: This Army-style aptitude test is for entertainment and self-testing only. It is not an official army test, recruitment assessment, military training, tactical guidance, or qualification. The quiz uses safe fictional scenarios built around focus, route sense, signals, supply logic, and calm judgment under pressure.

landing.quickStartText: The first drills feel simple. Then the mission clues start stacking up and the pressure kicks in.

stageGroups.title: Round 1: Spot the Smart Move
stageGroups.encouragement: You handled the first drills well. Most people start slipping once the details get messier.

questions.prompt: You reach a training building with two entrances. What is the smartest first move?
choices: Confirm which entrance the briefing means
Pick the nearest door and keep moving
Wait for someone else to choose

questions.prompt: A briefing says: map, water, signal card. At a route split, the signal card cannot be found. What should the team check before moving?
choices: Whether the signal card was packed
How fast the team can run

questions.prompt: A route card says Route Red is blocked. Which route should the team avoid?
Only checked bags get a white label. Bag 2 has a white label. What follows?
Remember this pair for later: Falcon - 6. Which number is paired with Falcon?
A signal flashes green, red, green, red, green. What comes next?
A signal sheet says Falcon means hold position. What should the team do if Falcon flashes?
choices: Push ahead before the route changes
Ignore the signal and finish loading

questions.prompt: Which choice best shows calm judgment?
A checklist says rope, map, gloves, water. At the first stop, the team only has rope, gloves, and water. What should be flagged before they continue?
choices: The water should be left behind

questions.prompt: A drill board says Checkpoint C opens last. The team reaches a locked gate marked C before the others open. What is the smartest read of the situation?
choices: Checkpoint C is probably not ready yet
Checkpoint C should be forced open first
Every checkpoint must already be open
The marker C probably means supplies

stageGroups.title: Round 2: Read The Route
stageGroups.encouragement: You are still on track to beat the 8%. The next round adds more route clues and signal pressure.

questions.prompt: On a simple grid, a marker starts at the center and moves one space north. Where is it now?
choices: One space left of the center

questions.prompt: A route note says the blue marker is the supply point. Which marker should the team move toward if they need supplies?
Remember this pair for later: Blue marker - 4. Which number is paired with Blue marker?
An order card says: start, blue point, supply square, finish. Which step comes after blue point?
A marker starts in the top-left cell of a 3 by 3 grid and moves one cell right. Where is it?
A marker starts at the center, moves one space south, then one space north. Where does it finish?
A signal pattern is short, long, short, long. What comes next?
Route Red is blocked, but the north path is clear. Which path is safer to name as usable?
choices: A shortcut no one has checked
Any path with dust on it

questions.prompt: A signal on the practice board is unclear. What is the best first action?
A message says, "Deliver the pack to the blue marker before Checkpoint C opens." Which location matters first?

stageGroups.title: Round 3: Pressure Decisions
stageGroups.encouragement: Good calls so far. This is where more than one option can sound plausible, but only one is the smart move.

questions.prompt: A map note and a supply note disagree on the practice board. What should happen before scoring?
A point marker is missing from the practice map. Which choice avoids a bad assumption?
choices: Ask for the marker position to be confirmed

questions.prompt: Blue marker is the supply point, Falcon means hold position, and Route Red is blocked. The team reaches Route Red while Falcon is showing. What should happen first?
choices: Push through Route Red before the route changes
Head for the blue marker immediately without stopping
Hold position and avoid Route Red
Ignore Falcon because the team is close

questions.prompt: A drill rule says to wait for a clear signal. The signal has not appeared. What is the best choice?
Checkpoint C opens last, but a fresh note tells the team to enter it now. What is the smartest response?
choices: Skip Checkpoint C for the whole mission

questions.prompt: A new note says Point C moved, but gives no new square. What is the strongest conclusion?
choices: The old location may now be unreliable

questions.prompt: Which detail matters most in a fast readiness check?
A calm teammate notices the plan may be wrong. What is the best next action?
A checked route shows a green light toward Checkpoint B. Another route heads to Checkpoint C, which opens last, but it is unconfirmed. Which option is most careful?
choices: Take the unconfirmed route because it might save time
Ignore both routes and wait forever
Use the checked route unless the other route is confirmed
Drive toward Checkpoint C and decide on arrival

questions.prompt: If only confirmed routes show a green light, and Route C has a green light, what can you safely conclude?

stageGroups.title: Round 4: Final Judgment Check
stageGroups.encouragement: You made it through the hardest checks. Your result is ready to reveal.

questions.prompt: Earlier, which number was paired with Blue marker?
A final plan card says Route Red is blocked, Falcon means hold, and Blue marker is the supply point. Which detail matters first if Falcon is flashing?
choices: The team should count packs first
Route Red might reopen by itself

questions.prompt: A marker starts at the center, moves north, east, south, then west. Where does it finish?
Falcon needs 6 packs, Blue marker needs 4 packs, and Route Red closing adds 2 extra packs to the same run. How many packs must that run carry?
Checkpoint C opens last, Blue marker is the supply point, and Falcon means hold. The team reaches Blue marker early while Falcon is flashing. What is the better move?
choices: Unload the packs and rush Checkpoint C immediately
Hold position near Blue marker and wait for the next clear instruction
Switch to Route Red because it is the direct route
Leave the packs and look for a new marker

questions.prompt: All confirmed paths have a check number. Path K has no check number. What can you safely say?
choices: Path K is not confirmed by that rule

questions.prompt: Earlier, which route was marked as blocked?
A route check takes 4 minutes, a signal check takes 3, and loading the Falcon and Blue marker packs takes 5. How many minutes pass before the team can move?
Earlier in the quiz, what did a green light show?
Earlier, Falcon was paired with 6, Blue marker was paired with 4, Blue marker was the supply point, and Route Red was blocked. If Falcon is flashing during the final run, what is the smartest call?
choices: Push through Route Red and deliver faster
Hold position, avoid Route Red, and protect the supply run
Ignore Falcon because the packs are already loaded
Skip the blue marker and go straight to Checkpoint C
